messages.subject: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
messages.subject_clean: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
messages.body_plain:
Hi!
I would like to make interactive simulation where simulation runs N steps at a time and user could interact with it by removing/adding/changing resources. I would use shiny and reactiveTimer to make the simulation run.

Is it possible to run simulation for some steps, then change/add/remove resources and then continue running? Or do all resources have to be determined beforehand (either static or scheduled)? I am able to change e.g. resource capacity using functions and conditions based on values of selected resource, but I do not know how to take input from outside of the simulation between steps. Is this some how possible using global attributes?

1) Run simulation N steps
2) Allow user to a) add cashier, b) remove cashier
3) Run again
4) Allow change ...

I could also predermine e.g. 10 resource one of which has capasity of 1 and rest 0. Than user input would either increment one capasity from 0 to 1 (add resource) or decrease it from 1 to 0 (remove resource)

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] Re: Changing resourses manually during simulation to make interactive simulation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Nice to know you managed to make it work. Some additional clarifications:
Yes, you can run the simulation for some time and then add new resources.
You can even add generators and change trajectories in the middle of a simulation.
No, you can't delete resources...
but you can set the capacity (and/or the queue) to zero.
I would argue that it's probably better to add everything you may need at the beginning, and then just play with the capacities to open/close resources.
Iñaki

On Mon, 9 Mar 2020 at 14:35, Ville Pietiläinen <vhpi...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I managed to make it work. No idea if the approach is good or bad.
>
> First I add N resources, one with capacity 1 and rest with capacity 0. I make function that checks two global variables, returns 1/2 if one of those is TRUE and 0 otherwise. It also updates the TRUE variable to FALSE.
>
> open <- T
> close <- F
>
> openclose <- function() {
>   if (open) {
>     open <<- F
>     1
>   } else if (close) {
>     close <<- F
>     2
>   } else {
>     0
>   }
> }
>
> In trajectory I have a branch which determines using above function whether to open or close a resource
>
> branch(
>     openclose,
>     c(T, T),
>     trajectory() %>%
>       simmer::select(function() {
>         print(paste0("Opening ", res[min(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 0))]))
>         get_capacity(store, res)
>         res[min(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 0))]
>       }) %>%
>       set_capacity_selected(1),
>     trajectory() %>%
>       simmer::select(function() {
>         print(paste0("Closing ", res[max(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 1))]))
>         res[max(which(get_capacity(store, res) == 1))]
>       }) %>%
>       set_capacity_selected(0)
>   )
>
> This way user can between runs change open/close value and next arrival updates the capasities.
>
> Sorry for the messy explanation :)
>

I am able to change e.g. resource capacity using functions and conditions based on values of selected resource, but I do not know how to take input from outside of the simulation between steps. Is this some how possible using global attributes?

messages.subject: Modeling stand-by (ex: failure repair model with backup machine)
messages.subject_clean: Modeling stand-by (ex: failure repair model with backup machine)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to model a production line where 2 machine works simultaneously. If one of the machine fails then we have a backup replacement which can switch immediately. There are two scenarios to model:

1. After the failed machine is repaired, it works as a standby until the next failure of any of the functioning machine
2. As soon as the failed machine is repaired, it replaces the standby machine.

I am really beginner and couldn't figure out where I should put these conditions and how.

# A reproducible example: Here I modeled all three machine working simultaneously depending on one resource (repairman) and without putting above mentioned scenarios.

# Failure rates of Machine 1, 2 and standby (SB)
M1.lambda <- 0.03
M2.lambda <- 0.02
SB.lambda <- 0.01

# Repair rates
M1.mu <- 0.2
M2.mu <- 0.2
SB.mu <- 0.3

# Mean time to failure
M1.MTTF <- 1/M1.lambda
M2.MTTF <- 1/M2.lambda
SB.MTTF <- 1/SB.lambda

# Mean time to repair
M1.MTTR <- 1/M1.mu
M2.MTTR <- 1/M2.mu
SB.MTTR <- 1/SB.mu

simTime <- 1000
simNum <- 5

# Trajectories for repair
M1.Trajectory <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("Repairman", 1) %>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, M1.mu)) %>%
  release("Repairman", 1)

M2.Trajectory <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("Repairman", 1) %>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, M2.mu)) %>%
  release("Repairman", 1)

SB.Trajectory <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("Repairman", 1) %>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, SB.mu)) %>%
  release("Repairman", 1)

envs3 <- mclapply(1:10, function(i) {
  simmer("ex3") %>%
    add_resource("Repairman", queue_size = Inf) %>%
    add_generator("M1.failure", M1.Trajectory, function() rexp(1, M1.lambda)) %>%
    add_generator("M2.failure", M2.Trajectory, function() rexp(1, M2.lambda)) %>%
    add_generator("SB.failure", SB.Trajectory, function() rexp(1, SB.lambda)) %>%
    run(100000) %>%
    wrap()
})

Can someone help me with this? Is there some identical example from where I can learn? Thanks

Best regards,
Ariful Islam
